changes: Extended the pooled outcome clock from FY1988–2014 to FY1988–2019 using the accepted FYEAR observation-year definition and TIME=FYEAR−1988. Rebuilt historical and added observations together; preserved the FY1987 TXR lag input and all original sample, denominator, CTE, currency, and corporation screens.

Extended FUNDA through FYEAR 2019, quarterly and monthly security-price bounds through 2019, and SEC_IDHIST plus daily/monthly exchange-rate date bounds through 2020-12-31 because FYEAR 2019 DATADATEs extend to 2020-05-31. The native handoff confirms FYEAR 1988–2019 and TIME 0–31.

Retained the accepted pooled 1st/99th percentile winsorization before the ≥5 firm-history rule, pooled OLS with intercept, ivreg2 small-sample inference, and two-way firm/year clustered standard errors. Added computed Stata e(sample) counts by original and added FYEAR periods; no model term, estimator, fixed effect, or weight changed.
limitations: The accepted build’s current-header approximations remain: current FUNDA FIC=USA for historical FINC=0, undated COMPANY.STKO and FUNDA.CONM for historical ownership/name screens, and FUNDA/header CUSIP fallback where no unique effective SEC_IDHIST CUSIP is available. These are not dated historical classifications.

Bounded source checks found ambiguous source keys in added-period inputs: one standard-format FUNDA GVKEY×FYEAR duplicate key in each FY2015–2019; standard-format FUNDQ GVKEY×DATADATE duplicate keys by calendar year were 37 (2015), 30 (2016), 35 (2017), 29 (2018), and 12 (2019). The accepted build excludes ambiguous annual, quarterly, security, identifier, and FX join keys rather than choosing a new tie winner; no handoff GVKEY-year duplication or missing DV/TIME was reported.

The paper’s Section 3.1 reports 124,514 nonmissing one-year Δ/MVA1 observations, while the accepted predecessor construction had 118,611 common-eligible rows; Table 6 Panel C reports N=111,558 while the saved predecessor fit had N=106,162. These gaps remain unexplained and are not attributed to this extension. The new joint fit has N=121,240, including 107,604 original-period and 13,636 added-period rows.

The paper does not name the estimator beyond a regression on a linear trend or specify the exact two-way finite-sample correction, pooled versus period-specific percentile grouping, percentile algorithm, or cutpoint order. The accepted best-effort choices remain OLS via ivreg2 small, pooled SAS PCTLDEF=5 cutoffs before the five-row firm filter, and FYEAR as the observation clock.

The paper’s TXR meaning differs between Section 2.2 and Table 4, and its printed 34% interval says “1998 through 1992.” The accepted construction preserves these discrepancies and applies 34% to FY1988–1992 as its documented interpretation.
The assignment retains only the all-firms Table 6 Panel C fit. Its multinational/domestic subgroup fits and the article’s other tables are outside this predecessor scope and were not run here.

The new and saved coefficients do not hold the estimation sample fixed: the ≥5 observation firm rule and pooled winsorization cutoffs are recalculated on the joint FY1988–2019 sample. The 1,442-row increase in the FY1988–2014 part of e(sample) is therefore part of the pooled extension, not an isolated time-window-only coefficient change.

comparison.interpretation: The extended trend remains positive and is larger and more statistically precise under the retained ivreg2, small, two-way clustered inference. This is not a fixed-sample comparison: the accepted ≥5-observation firm rule and pooled 1st/99th percentile cutoffs are recomputed on the joint FY1988–2019 common-eligible sample; the extended fit retains 1,442 more FY1988–2014 estimation rows than the saved predecessor.
